title: Rigveda 5.68: To Mitra and Varuna
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.68: To Mitra and Varuna: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.68 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Mitra and Varuna. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 386v-387r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>pra vo̍ mi̱trāya̍ gāyata̱ varu̍ṇāya vi̱pā gi̱rā | mahi̍kṣatrāv ṛ̱tam bṛ̱hat ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>SING forth unto your Varuṇa and Mitra with a song inspired. They, Mighty Lords, are lofty Law
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 386v (numbered 59v by the scribe) (OPenn image 387, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.67.1 ‹-āśātheiti›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 387r (numbered 60r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.68.2 ‹-itighṛta-yonī mitraḥ ca ubhā›. Verse 5.68.1 ends on this page.
translation.edition_text: <sup>1</sup>pra | vaḥ | mitrāya | gāyata | varuṇāya | vipā | girā | mahi-kṣatrau | ṛtam | bṛhat

translation.original_ref: RV 5.68.2-5 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 6); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 387r
translation.original_text:
2sa̱mrājā̱ yā ghṛ̱tayo̍nī mi̱traś co̱bhā varu̍ṇaś ca | de̱vā de̱veṣu̍ praśa̱stā ||
3tā na̍ḥ śakta̱m pārthi̍vasya ma̱ho rā̱yo di̱vyasya̍ | mahi̍ vāṁ kṣa̱traṁ de̱veṣu̍ ||
4ṛ̱tam ṛ̱tena̱ sapa̍nteṣi̱raṁ dakṣa̍m āśāte | a̱druhā̍ de̱vau va̍rdhete ||
5vṛ̱ṣṭidyā̍vā rī̱tyā̍pe̱ṣas patī̱ dānu̍matyāḥ | bṛ̱hanta̱ṁ garta̍m āśāte ||
translation.text:
2Full springs of fatness, Sovran Kings, Mitra. and Varuṇa, the Twain, Gods glorified among the Gods.
3So help ye us to riches, great terrestrial and celestial wealth: Vast is your sway among the Gods.
4Carefully tending Law with Law they have attained their vigorous might. The two Gods wax devoid of guile.
5With rainy skies and streaming floods, Lords of the strength that bringeth gifts, A lofty seat have they attained.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 387r (numbered 60r by the scribe) (OPenn image 387, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.68.2 ‹-itighṛta-yonī mitraḥ ca ubhā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 387v (numbered 60v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.69.2 ‹-tisṝṇām dhiṣaṇānām retaḥ-dhāḥ vi›. Verses 5.68.2-5 end on this page; 5.68.2 begins on fol. 386v (numbered 59v by the scribe).
translation.edition_text:
2sam-rājā | yā | ghṛtayonī itighṛta-yonī | mitraḥ | ca | ubhā | varuṇaḥ | ca | devā | deveṣu | pra-śastā
3tā | naḥ | śaktam | pārthivasya | mahaḥ | rāyaḥ | divyasya | mahi | vām | kṣatram | deveṣu
4ṛtam | ṛtena | sapantā | iṣiram | dakṣam | āśāteiti | adruhā | devau | vardheteiti
5vṛṣṭi-dyāvā | rīti-āpā | iṣaḥ | patī iti | dānu-matyāḥ | bṛhantam | gartam | āśāteiti
